source_notes.finding: No generated stubs. The sandbox gets exactly one host function, call_tool(tool_name, params), passed to Monty as an external function. The execute tool's description says so: 'Only `call_tool(tool_name: str, params: dict) -> Any` is available in scope.' Tool results come back as structured_content when the tool has an output schema, else as concatenated text.

The transform replaces the whole tool list with discovery tools plus execute. Defaults are Search (BM25 over the catalog, 'brief' names and descriptions) and GetSchemas ('detailed' parameter markdown); GetTags and ListTools are opt-in. So schemas load on demand, and the model never sees every schema up front unless ListTools(detail='full') is added.

call_tool is an async Python callback that Monty's worker invokes over its host channel. On the host it looks the tool up in the auth-filtered catalog and runs ctx.fastmcp.call_tool, so the real tool, and any credentials it holds, stay in the server process. Concurrent un-awaited calls work: asyncio.gather of 5 lookups took 215 ms host-side (P9).

Two layers. Language: Monty has no urllib/socket (P3 ModuleNotFoundError), refuses os.environ (P5), denies open('/etc/hosts') (P4 PermissionError), and has no __class__ on tuples or __import__ (P12). Process: each execute creates a new AsyncMonty pool whose worker is a separate `monty subprocess` process. The docs and the SandboxProvider docstring tell implementers never to use plain exec() for this untrusted code.

source_notes.finding: The caller gets only the last expression's value or `return` (P2 returned 'RETURNED' and 0 of 200,000 A's). feed_run is called without print_callback, and pydantic-monty's documented default is the host process stdout/stderr, so sandbox prints land in the server's log. Over stdio transport they appeared on the server's stderr, not on the JSON-RPC channel, and the session kept working.

source_notes.finding: Monty limits that CodeMode sets by default: max_feed_duration_secs=30 and max_memory=100 MB. It sets no max_turn_duration_secs, no gc_interval, and leaves max_recursion_depth at Monty's standard 1,000. limits=None disables time, memory and GC limits. Unknown keys raise ValueError. CodeMode adds max_tool_calls=50 and an optional wall_clock_timeout_secs (default None), which is the only bound on time spent inside host tools.
Fresh per execute: a new pool and a new checkout every call, so P8 printed 'gone'.

Sandbox exceptions surface as a tool error 'Error calling tool 'execute': ValueError: probe-boom'. The type and message survive; no line number or traceback (P10). Failed call_tool calls raise with the tool's parameter list appended when the failure looks like a validation error.

Median 7.7 ms per execute through the in-process client in the final run_all.sh rerun (P11). An earlier run under heavier load from the other workers measured 51.1 ms, so the number is load-sensitive. A new AsyncMonty pool plus feed alone costs a median 6.0 ms versus 0.10 ms on a reused session (out/P11-breakdown.txt), so spawning the per-call `monty subprocess` worker is most of the cost.

Apache-2.0, repo pushed 2026-11-22. The feature lives under fastmcp.experimental. Tools reach the sandbox through the same auth-filtered catalog the client would see (get_tool_catalog(ctx)), so visibility rules carry over.

surprises: print() output is silently dropped from the result. The docs example only uses `return`, but SPEC-style print-based code returns an empty result while the text goes to the server's own stdout/stderr (P1 print, P2).

Each execute spawns a fresh `monty subprocess` worker pool, so there is a process boundary as well as the interpreter boundary. Neither the FastMCP docs page nor code_mode.py says so; it comes from pydantic-monty 1.6.0's AsyncMonty.

The default time limit does not bound host tool time: feed duration excludes time awaiting call_tool, and wall_clock_timeout_secs defaults to None. The docs say this plainly, so it is a design choice, not a mismatch.
The tool-call cap error reaches the caller as 'Exception: Tool call limit exceeded...', losing the ToolError type (Pcap).
